chief_complaint: painless firm brown leg bump that dimples when pinched
hpi_details: A 77-year-old male presents to the clinic with painless firm brown leg bump that dimples when pinched. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks the hard bump is an old bug bite or thorn from his garden that became embedded and scarred over under the skin.
concerns: He is worried it is a malignant melanoma that has already spread internally, which might explain why he has felt so tired lately.
expectations: He hopes the doctor will examine the bump with a magnifying scope and confirm that he will not need surgery to cut it out.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Dermatofibroma is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Dermatofibroma: Reassure, no treatment needed unless symptomatic, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Melanoma (especially if changing) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.

Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

teaching.one_liner: A benign fibrous skin nodule, classically presenting as a painless, firm, brown bump on the leg that dimples inward when pinched (the 'dimple sign').
red_flags: Recent rapid growth or color change — would warrant biopsy to exclude melanoma

must_ask.say: When you pinch the sides of the bump, does it dimple inward?
How long have you had it, and has it grown?
Do you remember any injury or insect bite at that spot before it appeared?

history.answer: I noticed a firm, brownish bump on my lower leg recently, and I came in to get it checked out.
I first noticed it a few months ago, and over the past several weeks it has seemed slightly more prominent.
It is located right on the front part of my right lower leg, along the shin.
It started as a tiny spot and grew slowly to about the size of a pencil eraser, but it has not grown rapidly.
There is only this single bump on my right leg; I do not have any other bumps or spots elsewhere.
It feels very firm and hard like a small pebble under the surface, but it moves along with the skin.
When I pinch the skin on both sides of the bump, it dimples and puckers inward instead of popping outward.
No, it does not hurt at all, even when I touch it or press firmly on it.
It has stayed a steady light brownish color with smooth, regular borders; it has not turned jet black or uneven.
No, it has never bled, cracked open, oozed, or formed any scabs.
There is no redness around it, no swelling, no warmth, and never any discharge.
No, there is no blackhead or hole in the center, and nothing white or cheesy ever comes out.
No, it stays the exact same size; walking, standing, or resting does not make it change.
I think I may have had a minor bug bite or scratched that spot a while back, but there was no major trauma or cut.
I have felt some generalized fatigue recently, but I have not had any fever, chills, night sweats, or unexpected weight loss.
I usually wear long pants and have never had extensive sun exposure or severe blistering sunburns on my legs.
Neither I nor anyone in my family has ever had melanoma or any other type of skin cancer.
No, I do not take immunosuppressive medications, have never had an organ transplant, and do not have diabetes.
I have not squeezed, punctured, or applied any medicated ointments to it, and it has never been treated before.
I figured it was probably an old bug bite or thorn from working in the garden that got buried and hardened up.
I'm worried it might be a dark skin cancer like melanoma that's spreading, which could explain why I've been feeling so worn out lately.
I'm hoping you can look at it with your magnifying scope today and tell me I won't need to have a chunk of my leg carved out.
I have no chronic medical conditions, no high blood pressure, and no heart disease.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been hospitalized.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or vitamins.
I have no known allergies to medications, foods, or materials.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco.
I only drink an occasional glass of beer or wine at social gatherings, once or twice a month.
I am retired and live at home with my wife.
My parents lived into old age without any history of skin cancers or serious genetic conditions.

exam.finding: Alert, elderly male resting comfortably in no acute distress.
Blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 36.6 C, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.

Discrete 6 mm firm, non-tender, hyperpigmented tan-brown dermal nodule on the right anterior lower leg with regular borders; lateral pinching of the lesion causes it to tether and dimple downward beneath the skin surface.
Both lower extremities show symmetric calves without localized swelling, erythema, warmth, or tenderness.
No inguinal lymphadenopathy or tenderness bilaterally.
